merger_description:
Crestlink Koolan Pty Ltd (**Crestlink Koolan**) proposes to acquire 100% of the shares in MGX Resources Limited's (**MGX**) wholly owned subsidiary, Aztec Resources Limited, which through its subsidiaries holds the Koolan Island iron ore mining assets (the **Acquisition**).

Crestlink Koolan is part of the Crestlink Group. The Crestlink Group is an Australian infrastructure and logistics provider with a focus on the Kimberley region and northern Australia. The Crestlink Group is backed by US infrastructure investor Cerberus Capital Management LP.

Koolan Island has approached the natural end of its iron ore production and shipping operations, which were completed in July 2026. As part of the Acquisition, Crestlink Koolan will assume responsibility for the remaining mine rehabilitation obligations at Koolan Island. MGX is already undertaking substantial earthworks to remediate disturbed areas, with the remaining rehabilitation obligations at completion primarily related to the site's key infrastructure assets. Crestlink Koolan is establishing a logistics hub in the Kimberley region.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
certain publicly available information, and had regard to the factors
in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010
(Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between the Crestlink Group
(and its connected entities) and Aztec Resources in the
supply of air and marine infrastructure and logistics services
in Australia
b. there are several alternative suppliers of air and marine
infrastructure and logistics servicing the Kimberley region of
Western Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
